Since $\hat{\mathbf{N}}_g = (0,1)$, this is equivalent to finding the root of the x-component of $\hat{\mathbf{H}}$ [S1].

The claim states that since the normal vector N_g is (0,1), finding the root of the x-component of H is equivalent to the problem. The evidence in Source [S1] explicitly sets N_g = (0,1) and states: 'Then we need only search for x such that H = -N_g. Since we already know H and N_g lie in the z = 0 plane, this is equivalent to letting f(x) = (H .(1,0))...'. The dot product with (1,0) extracts the x-component. Since N_g has no x-component, the condition H = -N_g implies H_x = 0. Thus, finding the root of the x-component of H is indeed equivalent to the condition described.
